title: Whitechapel
subtitle: The Sixth Murder
description: A case for two investigators. Whitechapel, November 1888: an evening’s lodging becomes an enquiry into a woman’s death and the life she meant to begin. An original fictional mystery set against the historical murder enquiry.

orders-original.description: Abberline’s orders, Temporary assignment. Fictional illustrated original.

inn-newspaper-original.description: A fictional sensational newspaper. The woodcut shows a clothed, non-graphic figure with a scarf laid across her face. This is an invented report and illustration, not a reproduction of an actual issue.

travel-sleeve-original.description: A small stiff card railway ticket rests beside its folded paper sleeve. The passenger name is handwritten on the sleeve, not printed on the ticket.

sister-letter-original.description: Nora’s Bristol journey, A place in Bristol. Fictional illustrated original.

work-correspondence-original.description: Maggie’s work note, Work left at the workshop. Fictional illustrated original.

torn-wedding-front.description: Nora stands beside her mother in a formal studio wedding portrait. The right-hand portion, where another person stood, has been torn away. The surviving portion does not identify the missing man.

torn-wedding-back.description: The handwritten date is intact on the reverse of the surviving card. No groom’s name remains.

finch-work-card-original.description: An ordinary work card from before the wedding, kept with Maggie’s older accounts.

complete-wedding-front.description: The same wedding portrait as Nora’s torn print. Nora stands between her mother and Arthur Vale. Arthur is visibly the visitor interviewed at the Lantern. Maggie’s identification supplies the names and occasion.

complete-wedding-back.description: The couple’s names, wedding date and dedication are handwritten on the reverse.

medical-findings-original.description: Alden’s signed findings: fatal blunt head injury, post-mortem knife wounds. Fictional illustrated original.

burned-report-original.description: A partly burned portion of another copy of the inn newspaper. Enough of the masthead, date, article and scarf illustration remains to compare the edition. This is not a piece torn from the inn’s complete copy.

closing-letter-original.description: Maggie’s letter to Nora’s sister, From the Lantern. Fictional illustrated original.

lantern-cover.description: The fictional Lantern inn on the evening before the enquiry.

trunk-closed.description: A large, travel-worn wooden trunk with iron corners and leather straps, closed beside the Lantern service entrance. Long enough to contain a curled adult; no body shown.

trunk-open.description: The same open trunk with a few loose travelling clothes on top. Do not expose the concealed bedding yet.

trunk-bedding.description: The same trunk after lifting the loose clothes: folded wool bed blanket and pale lining with dark dried blood stains. No body, wounds or gore.

cart-sacks.description: A coal cart in a brick yard, dusty sacking covering its load. No horse attached; wheels have not moved since last night.

candlestick-recovered.description: A heavy brass chamber candlestick beneath a lifted coal sack, with a visibly bent loop handle and blue wax pooled in its dish.

room-packing.description: Nora’s small rear bedroom: clothes emptied beside a narrow bed, missing blanket, displaced rag rug and a vacant ring on the bedside table.

room-blood.description: The same bedroom with a corner of the rag rug lifted, revealing a small dark dried blood stain on floorboards. No violence or body shown.

sewing-case.description: Nora’s small wooden sewing case, needles, thread, cloth scraps; the torn wedding print lies inside its lid.

service-route.description: Architectural view from the rear service landing down three broad shallow steps to the yard, with room for the large trunk and a projecting washhouse screening the far discovery corner.

window-view.description: View from Baines’s low rear window: the landing and upper broad steps are visible, but the washhouse hides the discovery corner. Do not show the corner through walls.

hearth-surface.description: Cold hearth in Arthur’s lodgings, burned wool clothing and partly burned newspaper among ash. No knife, sheath or clasp.

hearth-clothing.description: Fire-damaged scraps of wool clothing among the ash. Dark stains are not forensically identified. No knife or sheath.

unfinished-work.description: Maggie’s long workshop table with unfinished shirt seams, thread and scissors; practical late Victorian garment work.

opening-sewing.description: A repaired dark sleeve beside Nora’s sewing case on the common-room table. Small careful stitches, work just completed.

opening-trunk.description: Nora’s large strapped travelling trunk near the service entrance before departure, clean and closed; ordinary luggage in use.

opening-candlestick.description: Brass chamber candlestick in ordinary evening use, bent loop handle and blue wax, carried towards Nora’s rear room.

yard-discovery.description: Empty screened corner of the inn yard after official removal, damp brick and very little visible blood. No body and no scarf left behind.

alden-candle-reassure.text: Yes. Something of this weight and shape could have done it.

alden-candle-reassure-turn-2.text: No. I’d be going further than the injury suggests. Where it came from, and who handled it—that may help you more.

alden-findings-reassure.text: Yes. I’ve finished writing up my notes.

alden-findings-reassure-turn-2.text: The injury to her head. A hard, blunt blow. There were also knife wounds.

alden-findings-reassure-turn-4.text: No. Those were inflicted after death. They did not kill her.

alden-findings-reassure-turn-6.text: Yes. I can establish that sequence. I cannot give you a precise hour, or name the particular object used for the blow.

alden-findings-reassure-turn-8.text: I understand why. But the appearance of this case is misleading. Here are my findings.

alden-greeting.text: Inspectors. Come in. We can speak here.

alden-knife-reassure.text: No. The knife wounds were made after death. The injury to her head killed her.

alden-knife-reassure-turn-2.text: I cannot identify a particular knife from those wounds.

alden-room-claim.text: Was there much where she was found?

alden-room-reassure.text: Then I’d look closely at the room. What you describe would fit her being injured there and carried out afterwards.

alden-room-reassure-turn-2.text: It’s possible. The blood on the bedding would fit that.

arthur-inn-greeting.text: Arthur Vale. Nora’s brother. The constable said I should speak to you.

arthur-inn-relationship-claim.text: That she was found in the yard. He wouldn’t tell me much else. What happened to her?

arthur-inn-relationship-reassure.text: Last night. I came here to speak to her.

arthur-inn-trunk-claim.text: No. I didn’t touch the trunk.

arthur-inn-trunk-followup-challenge.text: I didn’t. She saw someone else.

arthur-inn-trunk-followup-challenge-turn.text: No. I can only tell you it wasn’t me.

arthur-inn-trunk-followup-claim.text: Then she can’t tell you who it was.

arthur-inn-trunk-followup-reassure.text: I thought you meant this morning. Yes, I brought it down last night.

arthur-inn-trunk-followup-reassure-turn-.text: She was still packing. I was helping her with the luggage.

arthur-inn-trunk-followup-unsupported.text: You’ve shown me nothing that says I carried it.

arthur-inn-trunk-reassure.text: A carman. George, I think. She said it was arranged.

arthur-inn-trunk-reassure-turn-2.text: No. There was a cart in the yard. I took it to be his.

arthur-inn-trunk-reassure-turn-4.text: Nothing comes to mind. If it does, I’ll tell you.

arthur-inn-trunk-reassure-turn-6.text: I’ll be here. What happens about her things?

arthur-inn-trunk-reassure-turn-8.text: Of course. Just let me know when we can make the arrangements.

arthur-inn-visit-reassure.text: I thought she was rushing into it. She thought I ought to mind my own business.

arthur-inn-visit-reassure-turn-2.text: More than I should have. You don’t think it’ll be the last time you speak to someone, do you?

arthur-inn-visit-reassure-turn-4.text: She was packing. I wasn’t getting anywhere, so I left her to it.

arthur-inn-visit-reassure-turn-6.text: I didn’t look at a clock. I’m sorry.

arthur-station-candlestick-claim.text: Then why isn’t George sitting here?

arthur-station-candlestick-reassure.text: It was under the sacks in his cart. You ought to be asking him.

arthur-station-cause-challenge.text: And you’re saying that was me?

arthur-station-cause-challenge-turn-2.text: She didn’t see me hurt Nora. Nobody did.

arthur-station-departure-challenge.text: If she’d stopped and thought about it, yes.

arthur-station-departure-challenge-turn-.text: Her sister had been encouraging her. Nora wouldn’t have done this on her own.
You spoke to her for a few minutes. She was my wife.
She told me to leave. I wanted to talk.

arthur-station-departure-claim.text: I didn’t think I needed an invitation to speak to my wife.

arthur-station-departure-reassure.text: That she could come home. We could sort it out between ourselves.

arthur-station-departure-reassure-turn-2.text: She’d made up her mind. Bristol, her sister, this job. She wouldn’t listen to reason.

arthur-station-departure-reassure-turn-4.text: There was work here. She was throwing our marriage away.

arthur-station-departure-reassure-turn-6.text: Yes. I wanted her to hear me out.

arthur-station-departure-unsupported.text: What has that got to do with her going to Bristol?

arthur-station-disguise-challenge.text: They were going to blame me. You would have. Her husband, after an argument.

arthur-station-disguise-challenge-turn-2.text: I thought you might. If she was out there, like the woman in the paper.

arthur-station-disguise-challenge-turn-4.text: I’m not saying anything about that.

arthur-station-disguise-claim.text: She was my wife. I didn’t want people staring at her.

arthur-station-disguise-press.text: That’s what you think. I’ve told you why I covered her.

arthur-station-disguise-unsupported.text: Show me the illustration you mean.

arthur-station-finding-nora-reassure.text: I waited outside the workshop. Followed her when she left.

arthur-station-finding-nora-reassure-tur.text: She wouldn’t have spoken to me if she had.
When I went to her room. She said she was leaving in the morning.

arthur-station-fire-challenge.text: I don’t remember which clothes I put in.

arthur-station-fire-challenge-turn-2.text: Yes. I’m not denying I lit a fire.

arthur-station-fire-claim.text: I was clearing some things out.

arthur-station-fire-reassure.text: I’d been meaning to do it.

arthur-station-fire-reassure-turn-2.text: They were worn out. That’s why I got rid of them.

arthur-station-fire-unsupported.text: That isn’t clothing from my fireplace.

arthur-station-greeting.text: How much longer are you keeping me here?

arthur-station-purpose-challenge.text: I couldn’t leave her on the floor.

arthur-station-purpose-challenge-turn-2.text: I was frightened. I thought if I got her out of there, I’d have time to think.

arthur-station-purpose-challenge-turn-6.text: I covered her face. I couldn’t bear to look at her.

arthur-station-purpose-claim.text: I don’t want to go through it again.

arthur-station-purpose-press.text: You keep telling me what I did. Why bother asking?

arthur-station-purpose-unsupported.text: You said you had found something in the trunk. What was it?

arthur-station-relationship-challenge-tu.text: Because the moment I said husband, you’d stop looking for anyone else.

arthur-station-relationship-reassure.text: And why would she say that?

arthur-station-relationship-reassure-tur.text: I don’t know what Nora’s been telling people.

arthur-station-relationship-unsupported.text: Where’s the complete photograph she says she has?

arthur-station-room-reassure-turn-4.text: Then it could have been after I’d gone.

arthur-station-room-revisit-challenge.text: I took her arm. Just to stop her for a moment.

arthur-station-room-revisit-challenge-tu.text: She pulled back and fell against the washstand.
I didn’t mean for her to fall. She pulled so hard.
I thought she was dead. I didn’t know what to do.

arthur-station-room-revisit-claim.text: She wouldn’t stop to listen to me.

arthur-station-room-revisit-press.text: No. How many times do I have to say it?

arthur-station-room-revisit-unsupported.text: You said you were asking about her room.

arthur-station-source-reassure.text: I don’t remember. There were enough of you about.

arthur-station-source-reassure-turn-2.text: Someone told me. I wasn’t taking names.

arthur-station-source-rebuttal-challenge.text: I don’t have to remember every word everyone’s said to me today.

arthur-station-source-rebuttal-press.text: I’ve told you. Ask him again.

arthur-station-source-rebuttal-press-tur.text: Then I must have heard it from someone else. I don’t remember.

arthur-station-source-rebuttal-unsupport.text: You said you were asking about the candlestick.

arthur-station-trunk-disputing-challenge.text: No. She was doing it herself.
We had an argument. That’s all.

arthur-station-trunk-disputing-claim.text: And she didn’t see his face. You told me that.

arthur-station-trunk-disputing-reassure.text: No. I went to see her, and then I left.

arthur-station-trunk-disputing-reassure-.text: I didn’t carry it. I don’t know what else you want me to say.

arthur-station-trunk-disputing-unsupport.text: What’s that got to do with the trunk?

arthur-station-trunk-helping-challenge.text: Her things. That’s what I thought.

arthur-station-trunk-helping-claim.text: She was going away. I was helping.

arthur-station-trunk-helping-reassure-tu.text: Yes. I wasn’t watching everything she did.

arthur-station-trunk-helping-unsupported.text: You said there was blood in the trunk. Show me what you mean.

arthur-station-yard-challenge-turn-4.text: I read the paper. I didn’t do what was in it.

arthur-station-yard-claim.text: Of course. Everyone’s reading about the murders.

arthur-station-yard-reassure-turn-2.text: Then perhaps you ought to be looking for the man in the papers.

arthur-station-yard-unsupported.text: That’s not the newspaper you’re talking about.

baines-arrival-candle-claim.text: Nora’s room, out the back. She needs a candle.

baines-arrival-candle-reassure.text: Certainly not. It was knocked from a table years ago. The blue candles were cheap, so blue candles she shall have.

baines-arrival-greeting.text: Mr Reed and Mr Ellis? Come in out of the cold. Hale said to expect you.

baines-arrival-rooms-claim.text: You’ve the two rooms at the front. Breakfast’s at seven. Will you be wanting it earlier?

baines-arrival-rooms-press.text: You’ll be all right at the front. We sleep round the back. Just pull the door to gently when you go.

baines-arrival-rooms-press-turn-2.text: Enough to get the beds made. He said there’d be two of you, and here you are.

baines-arrival-rooms-reassure.text: Through there, then up the front stairs. If you need anything, my room’s down the back passage, beside Nora’s.

baines-arrival-rooms-reassure-turn-2.text: Best use the front. George is coming for Nora’s trunk in the morning. You’ll only be in each other’s way.

baines-blanket-challenge.text: That is Nora’s bed blanket. I know the blue border and that repair. It wasn’t travelling linen.

baines-blanket-reassure.text: Yes. Blue edging, and a darn by that corner.

baines-blanket-reassure-turn-2.text: On Nora’s bed. I made the bed myself.

baines-blanket-unsupported.text: Show me the bedding you mean. I cannot identify a blanket from another person’s account.

baines-cart-reassure.text: I arranged his paid job: carry Nora’s trunk in the morning. He left the cart after delivering coal and took the horse away.

baines-cart-reassure-turn-2.text: No. Anyone in the yard could reach the sacks. He had not moved it when he found Nora.

baines-disturbance-challenge.text: I can see that. But you’ll go away when you’ve finished here.

baines-disturbance-challenge-turn-2.text: Wouldn’t you be? With what’s happened to that girl?

baines-disturbance-claim.text: I only lent her a candlestick. I don’t look inside lodgers’ trunks.

baines-disturbance-press.text: Please. I’ve said all I can.

baines-disturbance-reassure-turn-2.text: The man who’s been killing those women. You haven’t caught him, have you?

baines-disturbance-unsupported.text: I don’t know what you want me to say about that.

baines-friend-reassure.text: Maggie Shaw, at the workshop. They worked together. You could try there.

baines-greeting.text: She was all ready to go. I was expecting her down this morning.

baines-hiding-claim.text: Drew back. Put the bolt across my door.

baines-hiding-reassure.text: After that cry? I was terrified. And then this morning they found her.

baines-hiding-reassure-turn-2.text: No. I kept away from the window. The washhouse hides that end of the yard anyway.

baines-identify-candle-challenge.text: It was. I lent it to her last night. That bent handle is unmistakable to me.

baines-identify-candle-challenge-turn-2.text: No. I did not see what happened behind the washhouse.

baines-identify-candle-reassure.text: Yes. The bend in the loop, and the blue wax. That is mine, from beside her bed.

baines-identify-candle-reassure-turn-2.text: No. I only know where I left it.

baines-identify-candle-unsupported.text: That is not the candlestick. Show me the object with the bent handle.

baines-identify-man-press.text: I didn’t see the man’s face. I can’t tell you whether it was Mr Vale.

baines-identify-man-reassure.text: I couldn’t recognise either voice. Please don’t put a name to him for me.

baines-missing-candle-claim.text: A heavy brass candlestick I lent her.

baines-missing-candle-reassure.text: A bent loop handle and blue wax. I took it in last night.

baines-missing-candle-reassure-turn-2.text: No. That empty ring on the little table is where it stood.

baines-safety-claim.text: He won’t leave while we’re talking?

baines-safety-reassure.text: Don’t let anyone come up behind me.

baines-safety-reassure-turn-2.text: All right. Shut that door, would you?

baines-sounds-claim.text: Voices, from the back. I was in my room.

baines-sounds-reassure.text: No. Then a cry. A thud, straight after it.

baines-sounds-reassure-turn-2.text: No. I stayed where I was.

baines-trunk-claim.text: Later I heard someone on the steps. I looked from my window.

baines-trunk-reassure.text: A man, carrying Nora’s trunk down.

baines-trunk-reassure-turn-2.text: No. He was turned away from me. I only had a glimpse.

baines-visitor-claim.text: Last night. I took a candlestick through to her room.

baines-visitor-reassure-turn-2.text: Just the candle. George was coming for her trunk in the morning.

cutscene-morning-0.text: Reed and Ellis leave through the front door and report to Commercial Street. Later, a message from Constable Hale brings them back to the Lantern.

cutscene-morning-1.text: Inspectors. The woman you met last night has been found dead. The doctor has attended; she has been taken to the mortuary.

cutscene-morning-2.text: We will need everyone’s account, and the things left where they were found.

cutscene-return-lantern-0.text: The report is complete. A police message has already been sent to Bristol. At the Lantern, Maggie has begun a personal letter to Nora’s sister.

cutscene-return-station-0.text: The recovered objects are brought to the station. The questions belong to the investigators, and the answers to Arthur.

cutscene-return-station-1.text: We have the case before us. Let him answer each part of it.

cutscene-search-arranged-0.text: The report is with the inspector. I’ll take Arthur to Commercial Street and keep him there while you search his lodging.

cutscene-search-arranged-1.text: Word has been sent to Bristol concerning Nora’s death. At Bell’s boot-repair shop, off Commercial Road, the landlord has admitted the officers to Arthur’s lodging.

cutscene-the-same-table-0.text: The newspaper lies set aside. Maggie returns to the letter.

cutscene-the-same-table-1.text: The common room carries on around the place where Nora worked.

detective-ellis-alden-candle-ask.text: Would you have a look at this?

detective-ellis-alden-candle-reassure.text: Under some sacks in the yard. Could it have caused the head injury?

detective-ellis-alden-candle-reassure-tu.text: Can you say whether this was the object used?

detective-ellis-alden-findings-reassure-.text: Did those contribute to her death?
People will think of the other murders.

detective-ellis-alden-knife-reassure.text: Hale found a knife beside Nora. Does that change your findings?

detective-ellis-alden-knife-reassure-tur.text: Can you identify that knife as the one used?

detective-ellis-alden-room-ask.text: There’s blood beneath the rug in her room. We found more inside her trunk, on the bedding.

detective-ellis-alden-room-reassure-turn.text: Thank you. We’re checking who handled it.

detective-ellis-arthur-inn-relationship-.text: We’re still establishing that. When did you last see her?

detective-ellis-arthur-inn-trunk-ask.text: Did you help take her luggage down?

detective-ellis-arthur-inn-trunk-followu.text: Mrs Baines saw a man carrying Nora’s trunk down last night. She couldn’t see his face.
You were there last night. Did you carry it down?
Could you have misunderstood us earlier? We meant last night, not this morning.

detective-ellis-arthur-inn-trunk-reassur.text: Is there anything else you can tell us about the evening?
We may need to speak to you again.
They’ll have to stay where they are for now.

detective-ellis-arthur-inn-visit-reassur.text: What did you say to that?
How were things when you left?
Can you tell us when that was?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-candlesti.text: We’ve recovered the candlestick Mrs Baines lent Nora.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-cause-ask.text: Hale recovered a knife beside Nora. Alden says it wasn’t what killed her.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-cause-cha.text: The blow to her head. The knife wounds were made after she was dead.
You argued with her. Baines heard a cry and a thud. You knew where the candlestick was hidden.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-departure.text: Had Nora asked you to come and see her?
She had her ticket and work arranged. Did you think she would stay?
Nora told us herself that she wanted the job.
And when you asked her to come home?
What did you want to say to her?
She told us she wanted the work.
Did she ask you to leave?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-disguise-.text: You say you covered her face because you couldn’t bear to look at her.
This is how the paper shows it. You’d read it, and then you left Nora like this in the yard.
So you wanted us to think it was him?
Alden says the blow killed her. Did you strike her with the candlestick?
You still haven’t explained how you knew where it was hidden.
You were trying to make it look like one of the other murders.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-finding-n.text: How did you know Nora was staying at the Lantern?
Did she know you were following her?
When did you learn about Bristol?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-fire-ask.text: You burnt clothing and a newspaper when you got home.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-fire-chal.text: We found these remains in your fireplace. Were they what you wore to see Nora?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-fire-reas.text: Was there something wrong with the clothes?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-purpose-a.text: You say Nora fell in her room. She was found outside. What happened in between?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-purpose-c.text: Her bedding was inside the trunk, stained with blood. The packing was left in her room.
So you put her in the trunk?
You took her into the yard.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-purpose-p.text: You put her in the trunk and carried her out, didn’t you?

detective-ellis-arthur-station-relations.text: We’ve spoken to Maggie Shaw. She says you were Nora’s husband.
Maggie kept this photograph of your wedding. Is that you beside Nora?
Nora and her mother. You’re on the right.
Why tell us she was your sister?
She says she attended your wedding.

detective-ellis-arthur-station-room-ask.text: What happened when Nora asked you to leave?

hale-discovery-reassure-turn-2.text: Beyond the washhouse. You can’t see the corner until you come into the yard.

hale-discovery-reassure-turn-4.text: She was lying there with her scarf across her face. I sent for Dr Alden.

hale-discovery-reassure-turn-6.text: He says it was already like that. Says he hadn’t touched it.

hale-discovery-reassure-turn-8.text: At the mortuary. Alden examined her in the yard first, then we brought a stretcher.

hale-greeting.text: Inspectors. Arthur is waiting here with me. A constable is keeping the yard clear.

hale-knife-reassure.text: A knife. It was out in the open beside her. I picked it up before they brought the stretcher. I’ve kept it wrapped here.

hale-knife-reassure-turn-2.text: Of course. I haven’t established who it belongs to.

hale-privacy-reassure.text: Moss, the doctor and the removal men. There’s a constable guarding the yard now. Arthur came after the removal; I’ve kept him here with me.

hale-privacy-reassure-turn-2.text: Understood. The rear passage is shut. Speak to Moss in the yard and Mrs Baines in her own room. I won’t let anyone go between them and Arthur.

hale-protection-reassure.text: I’ll put a constable at the back steps. Mrs Baines can see him from her window.

hale-protection-reassure-turn-2.text: Yes, sir. I’ll stay here with Arthur.

hale-station-disclosure-reassure.text: Only me, apart from you. I spoke to him at the front and brought him here myself.

hale-station-disclosure-reassure-turn-2.text: No, sir. I told him Nora had been found in the yard. Nothing about the cart search.

hale-station-disclosure-reassure-turn-4.text: No. I kept the rear passage shut. Moss spoke in the yard; an officer took him round to his horse and back without passing through the front. Mrs Baines spoke in her own room. Neither has been in to see him.

hale-station-disclosure-reassure-turn-6.text: The removal men left before he arrived. The yard constable and the officer checking his address kept away from him. He’s been with me throughout. Nobody else has spoken to him.

hale-station-greeting.text: Inspectors. I’m here if you need me.

maggie-brother-reassure.text: Arthur was her husband. I was at their wedding.

maggie-brother-reassure-turn-2.text: I’ve a photograph. You can see for yourselves.

maggie-closing-greeting.text: I’ve started three times. There is no decent first sentence for a letter like this.

maggie-closing-letter-reassure.text: You may. I have said the enquiry is complete, and that you will write to her.

maggie-closing-letter-reassure-turn-2.text: Her things, her work, the ticket. She should have been in Bristol by now.

maggie-closing-sister-claim.text: You’ve sent word. But she’ll want to hear from someone who knew Nora here.

maggie-closing-sister-press.text: Yes. I know where to send them. I’ll tell her the police are keeping them safe for now.

maggie-closing-sister-press-turn-2.text: Then I can write about Nora, instead of trying to explain every part of the enquiry.

maggie-closing-sister-reassure.text: I will. I’m telling her Nora had everything ready, and that her sewing case is here.

maggie-closing-sister-reassure-turn-2.text: She should have arrived with them herself.

maggie-marriage-reassure.text: Yes. I was at their wedding. I’ve a photograph. You can see for yourselves.

maggie-name-reassure.text: Finch was her name before she married. She wanted to use it again.

maggie-name-reassure-turn-4.text: Her old work card. It’ll be with the accounts.

maggie-photograph-reassure.text: Nora and her mother. Arthur on the right.

maggie-photograph-reassure-turn-2.text: Their wedding day. Eighth of June, four years ago. It’s written on the back.

maggie-privacy-challenge.text: Is Arthur outside? I need to know before I say anything else.

maggie-privacy-claim.text: Then it’s true. They said a woman had been found at the Lantern. Before I say anything—is Arthur with you?

maggie-privacy-press.text: That I helped her. She asked me to keep quiet until she was away.

maggie-privacy-press-turn-2.text: Please. Then I’ll tell you what I can.

maggie-privacy-reassure.text: Could you shut the door, please?

maggie-privacy-reassure-turn-2.text: Nora asked me to keep quiet until she was away. I helped her with a few things.

maggie-separation-reassure.text: She asked me not to say anything until she was away.

maggie-separation-reassure-turn-10.text: Above Bell’s boot-repair shop, off Commercial Road. The upstairs room.

maggie-separation-reassure-turn-14.text: Will someone tell her sister? She’ll be waiting at the station.

maggie-separation-reassure-turn-2.text: He’d come here for her wages. Wait outside when we finished. If she stopped to speak to someone, he wanted to know who.

maggie-separation-reassure-turn-4.text: Yes. The money, the waiting. What happened at home, I only know what she told me.

maggie-separation-reassure-turn-6.text: That she couldn’t go anywhere without having to explain herself afterwards. She wanted to leave, so I helped her take a few things to the Lantern.

maggie-separation-reassure-turn-8.text: I didn’t tell him. I don’t know what she said to him.

maggie-work-claim.text: At this table. That’s her work there. I haven’t moved it.

maggie-work-reassure.text: Yes. Worried about making a start somewhere new, of course. She kept asking whether they’d expect her to work faster.

maggie-work-reassure-turn-2.text: Not once she knew their ways. She was good.

nora-greeting.text: There’s room here. Mind the pins.

nora-journey-claim.text: Yes. Bristol. My sister’s found me work and a room near hers. The work’s a trial, anyway.

nora-journey-reassure.text: Yes. There’s no putting it off now.

nora-journey-reassure-turn-2.text: Seeing my sister, yes. Walking into a room full of women who’ve worked together for years… I’ll be glad when the first day’s over.

nora-journey-reassure-turn-4.text: One trunk. George is taking it to the station. My sewing things will come with me. I’d rather keep hold of those.

nora-paper-reassure.text: Is there any truth in this? About the murders?

nora-paper-reassure-turn-10.text: She’s already said she will. I’ve had two letters telling me where to stand.

nora-paper-reassure-turn-12.text: I shall. She’ll never let me hear the end of it otherwise. There. Mrs Baines can have her arm back.

nora-paper-reassure-turn-2.text: They make it sound as though he could walk into any street, kill another woman, then simply walk away.

nora-paper-reassure-turn-4.text: Mrs Baines reads every word. Then she tells me I shouldn’t worry.

nora-paper-reassure-turn-6.text: Not far. Far enough when there’s nobody about. Last night I heard someone behind me and crossed the road. It was a woman from the workshop.

nora-paper-reassure-turn-8.text: We did, after that. She’d been trying to catch me up. Neither of us fancied walking alone.

nora-work-claim.text: It’s Mrs Baines’s sleeve. She caught it on a nail and made it worse trying to get free.

nora-work-reassure.text: Nearly done. Though I did tell her the nail wants seeing to as well.

nora-work-reassure-turn-2.text: Yes. Mostly alterations. I’m starting at another place on Monday.

chapters.report: Arthur Vale is responsible for Nora Vale’s murder. The fatal blunt injury, room and trunk traces support an attack indoors followed by movement and concealment. Arthur knew the candlestick’s unshared hiding place; Hale’s checked account contradicts his claimed source. This knowledge strengthens the case built from his visit, argument, concealed marriage and changing answers. The newspaper and discovery comparison support deliberate imitation as the investigators’ inference unless Arthur separately admitted that purpose. george-night.title: George’s account of the night
george-night.description: George denies returning after taking the horse to its stable.
george-night.detail: He says he noticed no one coming or going, was occupied with the horse, heard nothing from inside and did not return until morning. His account is not an independently witnessed alibi for the whole night.
george-night.provenance: George Moss, account of his own movements

cart-access.title: The cart stood unguarded
cart-access.description: Baines confirms that George’s cart remained accessible overnight.
cart-access.detail: George left the cart after his coal delivery and took the horse away. Anyone who entered the yard could reach the sacks. Ownership of the cart does not identify whoever concealed an object there.
cart-access.provenance: Mrs Baines, collection and access account

george-candlestick.title: George’s answer about the candlestick
george-candlestick.description: George denies putting the candlestick under the sacks.
george-candlestick.detail: He says the cart stood there all night and that he found Nora before moving it. This is his answer to the recovery, not proof of who placed the object under the sacks.
george-candlestick.provenance: George Moss, questioned about the cart

arthur-brother.title: Arthur’s claimed relationship
arthur-brother.description: Arthur says he is Nora’s brother.
arthur-brother.detail: He uses the claimed relationship to request her belongings. The investigators have not released them to him.

arthur-visit.title: Arthur’s visit
arthur-visit.description: Arthur admits visiting and arguing about Nora’s journey.
arthur-visit.detail: He says she was packing when he left after a disagreement about Bristol and cannot give an exact time. This records Arthur’s claim; it does not establish it as fact.

arthur-trunk-denial.title: Arthur’s trunk denial
arthur-trunk-denial.description: Arthur says he did not touch or carry the trunk.
arthur-trunk-denial.detail: His initial account is a direct denial of moving Nora’s luggage from her room.

arthur-trunk-reply.title: Arthur’s answer about the trunk
arthur-trunk-reply.description: Arthur was asked about an unidentified man carrying the trunk.
arthur-trunk-reply.detail: The interview preserves whether Arthur conceded helping with luggage or maintained his denial. Baines did not identify him; her sighting alone cannot contradict that denial.
arthur-trunk-reply.provenance: Arthur Vale, follow-up at the Lantern

baines-last-seen.title: Baines’s last ordinary contact with Nora
baines-last-seen.description: Baines took a candlestick to Nora while she was packing.
baines-last-seen.detail: Nora asked for a candle. Baines mentions the luggage collection arranged for the morning. She does not identify a visitor.

baines-fear.title: Baines is afraid the man may return
baines-fear.description: Baines fears whoever killed Nora may come back.
baines-fear.detail: Questioning reveals her fear but does not establish what she heard or saw. Her suspicion of the Whitechapel murderer is a frightened belief, not an identification.
baines-fear.provenance: Mrs Baines, questions about the night

hale-private-recovery.title: Hale keeps the search private
hale-private-recovery.description: Arthur is kept at the front, away from the search and witness interviews.
hale-private-recovery.detail: Hale controls the rear passage. The detectives inspect the yard privately; George is questioned there and Baines in her own room. Neither witness is allowed to speak to Arthur. Recovery details are not discussed in his hearing.
hale-private-recovery.provenance: Constable Hale, access arrangements before the search

courtyard-knife.title: The knife recovered beside Nora
courtyard-knife.description: Hale found an ordinary knife openly beside Nora in the courtyard.
courtyard-knife.detail: Hale recovered the knife before the stretcher arrived and retains it wrapped for examination. Its owner is unknown. Its presence does not establish what killed Nora.
courtyard-knife.provenance: Constable Hale, recovery and custody account

hale-protection.title: A constable watches the back steps
hale-protection.description: Hale arranges for a constable to watch the back steps while Baines speaks.
hale-protection.detail: A constable watches the steps throughout the enquiry while Hale remains with Arthur at the front. The detectives can tell Baines what has actually been arranged.

baines-reassured.title: Baines agrees to speak
baines-reassured.description: Baines agrees to talk after hearing that a constable is watching the steps.
baines-reassured.detail: She asks to sit away from the passage with the door shut. No night observations are recorded until she gives them.

baines-disturbance.title: Voices, a cry and a thud
baines-disturbance.description: Baines heard voices, then a cry and a thud from the rear rooms.
baines-disturbance.detail: She could not make out the words or identify the speakers. She stayed in her room and did not open her door.
baines-disturbance.provenance: Mrs Baines, account given after reassurance

baines-trunk.title: An unidentified man carried the trunk
baines-trunk.description: Baines glimpsed a man carrying Nora’s trunk down the steps after the disturbance.
baines-trunk.detail: She looked from her window. The man was turned away and she could not see his face. This statement does not identify Arthur, George or the Whitechapel murderer.

baines-hiding.title: Baines bolted her door and hid
baines-hiding.description: Baines withdrew from the window and hid after seeing the man.
baines-hiding.detail: She feared he might be the Whitechapel murderer. She did not see what he did in the screened yard or what the trunk contained. There was no encounter or spoken threat.

blanket-identification.title: Nora’s bed blanket
blanket-identification.description: Baines identifies the stained blanket from the trunk as Nora’s bedding.
blanket-identification.detail: She recognizes the blue edging and a repair near one corner. The same blanket was on Nora’s bed, where it is now missing.
blanket-identification.provenance: Mrs Baines, shown the trunk bedding

candlestick-description.title: The missing bedside candlestick
candlestick-description.description: Baines describes the heavy candlestick she lent Nora.
candlestick-description.detail: It stood beside Nora’s bed. Its loop handle is bent and its dish holds blue wax. A description alone does not prove which object was used in an attack.

candlestick-identification.title: Baines identifies the candlestick
candlestick-identification.description: Baines recognizes the bent handle and blue wax on the recovered candlestick.
candlestick-identification.detail: The object recovered under the coal sacks is the candlestick she put beside Nora’s bed. Baines does not know who carried it into the yard.
candlestick-identification.provenance: Mrs Baines, shown the recovered object

workshop-lead.title: Maggie Shaw’s workshop
workshop-lead.description: Maggie Shaw can be found at the garment workshop.
workshop-lead.detail: The source of this lead is preserved in the discovery record: Baines’s directions or the work note in Nora’s room. Maggie worked with Nora.
workshop-lead.provenance: Lantern enquiries or Nora’s work correspondence

work-correspondence.title: Maggie’s work note
work-correspondence.description: A note in Nora’s room names Maggie Shaw’s garment workshop.
work-correspondence.detail: Maggie kept Nora’s unfinished work and said she would be at the long table by the workshop window.

trunk-interior.title: The stained trunk interior
trunk-interior.description: Loose clothes concealed stained bedclothes and lining.
trunk-interior.detail: The deep trunk is large enough for a curled adult. Dark blood stains mark the blanket and lining beneath a few clothes. Its contents and Hale’s separate-removal account must be considered together.
trunk-interior.provenance: Trunk beside the Lantern service entrance

cart-candlestick.title: Candlestick beneath the sacks
cart-candlestick.description: A heavy brass candlestick lay hidden in George’s coal cart.
cart-candlestick.detail: The loop handle is bent and blue wax fills the dish. This records the recovery place and appearance, not the owner or who concealed it.
cart-candlestick.provenance: Beneath a coal sack in George’s cart

yard-discovery.title: The screened discovery corner
yard-discovery.description: Very little blood remains at the discovery spot.
yard-discovery.detail: The projecting washhouse screens this corner from Baines’s window. Nora and her scarf have been removed; the scarf is retained with her effects.

room-disturbance.title: Interrupted packing and concealed blood
room-disturbance.description: Clothes lie emptied by the bed and blood is hidden beneath the rug.
room-disturbance.detail: A blanket is missing from the bed. The rug has been shifted over a dark blood stain. These are observations of a disturbance; the identity of the person responsible remains to be established.

torn-wedding.title: Nora’s torn wedding photograph
torn-wedding.description: A wedding portrait has been torn through the person beside Nora.
torn-wedding.detail: Nora and her mother remain. The reverse reads “Our wedding · 8 June 1884”. The surviving photograph does not identify the removed groom.

travel-papers.title: The ticket, sleeve and sister’s letter
travel-papers.description: Nora had prepared a Saturday journey to Bristol.
travel-papers.detail: The ordinary ticket is for the Bristol journey. The handwritten sleeve is addressed to Nora Finch; the sister’s letter offers sewing work and explains that Finch was used at Nora’s request.

service-route.title: The short service route
service-route.description: A short landing and a few broad steps connect the rear rooms to the yard.
service-route.detail: The route is wide enough for Nora’s large trunk. This establishes a possible route, not who used it.

window-view.title: What Baines’s window overlooks
window-view.description: The landing and upper steps are visible, but the discovery corner is screened.
window-view.detail: The projecting washhouse blocks the far corner. Baines could see a trunk being carried down without seeing its contents or what happened beyond the washhouse.

medical-findings.title: Alden’s medical findings
medical-findings.description: The blunt head injury was fatal; the knife wounds were inflicted after death.
medical-findings.detail: Alden establishes the head injury as fatal and the throat and abdominal wounds as post-mortem. He cannot identify a unique weapon or offender, or give a precise hour of death.
medical-findings.provenance: Dr William Alden, explanation and signed account

alden-knife.title: Alden on the recovered knife
alden-knife.description: The knife recovered beside Nora does not change Alden’s findings.
alden-knife.detail: Alden confirms the knife wounds were inflicted after death and cannot identify a particular knife from them.
alden-knife.provenance: Dr Alden, discussion after Hale’s knife recovery

alden-movement.title: Alden on the room and trunk
alden-movement.description: Alden considers the traces consistent with injury indoors and subsequent movement.
alden-movement.detail: The room blood and stained bedding support movement when read with the discovery account. His medical opinion does not identify the person who moved Nora.
alden-movement.provenance: Dr Alden, shown the room and trunk observations

alden-candlestick.title: The blunt-object comparison
alden-candlestick.description: Alden says the candlestick is consistent with a hard, blunt blow.
alden-candlestick.detail: He cannot uniquely identify this object as the cause of Nora’s head injury. The blunt head injury was fatal. Compatibility alone does not uniquely identify the candlestick as the weapon.
alden-candlestick.provenance: Dr Alden, shown the recovered candlestick

maggie-cooperation.title: Maggie agrees to speak
maggie-cooperation.description: Maggie agrees to speak privately after asking whether Arthur is present.
maggie-cooperation.detail: Maggie helped Nora with preparations and was asked to keep quiet until Nora was away. The investigators establish that Arthur has not come with them and close the workshop door.

finch-work-card.title: The earlier Finch work card
finch-work-card.description: Maggie’s older work card names Nora Finch before the wedding.
finch-work-card.detail: Maggie explains that Finch was Nora’s family name. Maggie names Arthur Vale as Nora’s husband. Nora was returning to Finch for the Bristol journey.

marriage-identification.title: Maggie identifies the marriage
marriage-identification.description: Maggie says Arthur Vale was Nora’s husband, not her brother.
marriage-identification.detail: She says she attended Nora and Arthur’s wedding. Her testimony establishes the marriage independently of examining the photograph. She is Nora’s friend and fellow worker; Nora’s sister lives in Bristol.
marriage-identification.provenance: Maggie Shaw, first-hand knowledge of the marriage

complete-wedding.title: The complete wedding photograph
complete-wedding.description: Arthur appears beside Nora in Maggie’s complete print.
complete-wedding.detail: The reverse names Nora Finch and Arthur Vale and gives their wedding date. Maggie identifies the couple and occasion while handing over her print; it can also be compared with the torn print if found.
complete-wedding.provenance: Maggie Shaw’s own keepsake, handed over for examination

maggie-separation.title: Why Nora left
maggie-separation.description: Maggie helped Nora leave Arthur and prepare for work near her sister.
maggie-separation.detail: Maggie says Arthur took Nora’s wages and checked where she went. Nora decided to leave. They had shared the upstairs room above Bell’s boot-repair shop, off Commercial Road. Maggie did not witness the killing.
maggie-separation.provenance: Maggie Shaw, account of helping Nora

address-verified.title: Hale’s address verification
address-verified.description: Hale confirms Arthur still occupies the room Maggie described.
address-verified.detail: The landlord at Bell’s boot-repair shop confirms Arthur’s current occupancy. This verifies where a search can be arranged; it supplies no prediction of what will be found.
address-verified.provenance: Constable Hale, relaying the checking officer’s report

unfinished-work.title: Nora’s unfinished allocation
unfinished-work.description: Careful seams stop partway through a pile of shirts.
unfinished-work.detail: The remaining allocation was left for the workshop when Nora prepared to travel. It supplies context for her trade and ordinary plans.

hearth-clothing.title: Burned clothing
hearth-clothing.description: Woollen clothing has been burned among the hearth remains.
hearth-clothing.detail: Stained cloth remains among the ash. This observation does not identify a particular stain by scientific test. The remains do not identify a particular wearer or a particular source of the stains.

burned-report.title: Arthur’s burned report
burned-report.description: A partly burned copy retains the dated report and scarf illustration.
burned-report.detail: The legible portion can be compared with the complete newspaper at the inn. It is another copy, not a fragment removed from the inn paper.

station-relationship.title: Arthur’s relationship explanation
station-relationship.description: Arthur was questioned about concealing his marriage.
station-relationship.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

station-trunk.title: Arthur’s account of the contents
station-trunk.description: Arthur was questioned about the stained trunk and his earlier answer.
station-trunk.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

station-fire.title: Arthur’s answer about the fire
station-fire.description: Arthur was questioned about the clothing and newspaper he burned.
station-fire.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

station-knowledge.title: Arthur’s answer about the unshared detail
station-knowledge.description: Arthur was confronted after Hale’s account contradicted his claimed source.
station-knowledge.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

station-room.title: Arthur’s account of the room
station-room.description: Arthur was asked what happened during his visit to Nora’s room.
station-room.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

station-cause.title: The fatal-injury allegation
station-cause.description: Arthur’s account was tested against the medical findings and the disturbance.
station-cause.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

station-yard.title: Arthur’s account of the yard
station-yard.description: The allegation that the yard was arranged to suggest another murder was put to Arthur.
station-yard.detail: The saved interview preserves the exact response obtained. This subject record does not assert an admission beyond those words.

arthur-candlestick-slip.title: Arthur names the hiding place
arthur-candlestick-slip.description: Arthur says the candlestick was under the sacks in George’s cart.
arthur-candlestick-slip.detail: Told only that the candlestick had been recovered, Arthur directs suspicion at George and volunteers the concealed location. This is evidence of knowledge, not an explicit confession to killing Nora.

arthur-source-claim.title: Arthur says an officer told him
arthur-source-claim.description: Arthur claims one of the officers told him where the candlestick was found.
arthur-source-claim.detail: He cannot name the officer and says someone told him rather than that he overheard it. This excuse remains to be checked with Hale.
arthur-source-claim.provenance: Arthur Vale, question about his source

hale-disclosure-check.title: Hale checks who spoke to Arthur
hale-disclosure-check.description: Hale says he did not disclose the candlestick’s hiding place to Arthur.
hale-disclosure-check.detail: Hale accounts for Arthur’s access and contacts: the removal officers left before Arthur arrived, Hale alone spoke to and escorted him, the yard and address officers kept away from him, and witness interviews and the search were kept separate. Read this with Arthur’s specific claim and the detectives’ own private questioning.

arthur-fall.title: Arthur claims Nora fell
arthur-fall.description: Arthur changes his account and says he took Nora’s arm before she fell.
arthur-fall.detail: He claims she pulled away and struck the washstand, then says he thought she was dead. This contradicts his earlier account of leaving her packing; it does not establish that her death was accidental.
arthur-fall.provenance: Arthur Vale, return to the argument

scarf-admitted.title: Arthur admits moving Nora and covering her face
scarf-admitted.description: Arthur says he moved Nora in the trunk and covered her face in the yard.
scarf-admitted.detail: He claims he was frightened and could not bear to look at her. This admission does not yet acknowledge an intention to imitate the murders.

disguise-admitted.title: Arthur’s account of the disguise
disguise-admitted.description: Arthur admits wanting the arrangement in the yard to suggest another Whitechapel murder.
disguise-admitted.detail: He acknowledges hoping the arrangement would divert blame to the other murderer, but refuses to discuss the knife and insists Nora fell. His last answer denies killing her. This is a limited admission to disguise, not a confession to the fatal blow.

arthur-found-nora.title: How Arthur found the Lantern
arthur-found-nora.description: Arthur says he followed Nora from the workshop on Friday.
arthur-found-nora.detail: He says Nora did not know he was following her and that he learned about Bristol when he went to her room. This records his account of finding her, not an admission to the killing.

arthur-departure.title: Arthur wanted Nora to return
arthur-departure.description: Arthur says he wanted Nora to come home.
arthur-departure.detail: He says Nora asked him to leave, but he stayed to talk. He blames her decision to leave or her sister’s encouragement; the detectives put Nora’s own plans to him.

closing-addressed.title: The people waiting at the Lantern
closing-addressed.description: An investigator has spoken with someone left waiting for news.
closing-addressed.detail: The closing conversation remains in the shared interview record. Nora’s belongings remain secured as evidence pending arrangements with her sister.

closing-letter.title: Maggie writes to Nora’s sister
closing-letter.description: Maggie’s letter turns to Nora’s belongings and interrupted journey.
closing-letter.detail: The letter says the enquiry is complete without inventing an admission from Arthur. Maggie will help return Nora’s things when they may be released.

deductions.title: The trunk carried out at night
deductions.question: Why was Nora’s trunk carried out during the night?
deductions.explanation: The man carried the trunk after an indoor disturbance. Its stained bedding and lining, with the room traces, support moving Nora into the yard. This raises a question about concealment behind the apparent street murder. It neither identifies the man nor rules out the Whitechapel murderer.

deductions.title: Movement from room to yard
deductions.question: Was Nora moved from her room?
deductions.explanation: Blood beneath the rug, emptied packing and stained trunk bedding support movement from the room to the yard. Baines identifies the missing blanket and the inspected service route can accommodate the trunk.

deductions.title: The concealed marriage
deductions.question: Who was Arthur to Nora?
deductions.explanation: The complete wedding print and Maggie’s identification establish that Arthur was Nora’s husband. His morning brother claim concealed that relationship while he sought control of her belongings. Baines did not admit him under that claim the night before.

deductions.title: The missing candlestick recovered
deductions.question: Where did the candlestick in the cart come from?
deductions.explanation: Baines identifies the recovered candlestick as the one she placed in Nora’s room. Its recovery proves concealment in the cart, not that George hid or used it.

deductions.title: After the disturbance
deductions.question: What did Baines hear and see?
deductions.explanation: Baines heard voices, a cry and a thud, later glimpsed an unidentified man carrying Nora’s trunk, then bolted her door and hid. The observations support a sequence, not the carrier’s identity or an eyewitness account of the killing.

deductions.title: Another copy of the same report
deductions.question: Which report did Arthur possess?
deductions.explanation: The surviving masthead, date, text and illustration identify another copy of the same edition. The inn’s complete copy never left the common room. Ownership alone does not prove murder or imitation.

deductions.title: The misleading knife
deductions.question: Did the knife beside Nora cause her death?
deductions.explanation: The openly placed knife and visible wounds suggest a knife killing. Alden establishes that the blunt head injury killed Nora and that the knife wounds were made after death. This distinguishes the fatal assault from the later injuries; the arrangement’s purpose and its author require further evidence.

deductions.title: Arthur knows the hiding place
deductions.question: What did Arthur know that the detectives had not told him?
deductions.explanation: Arthur volunteered that the candlestick was under the sacks in George’s cart. The detectives had disclosed only its recovery. His accurate description of the concealed location requires an explanation; it is not itself a complete confession.

deductions.title: The officer explanation fails
deductions.question: Does Hale’s account support Arthur’s claimed source?
deductions.explanation: Arthur says an officer told him where the candlestick was found. Hale accounts for his contacts and confirms that no such disclosure occurred. Combined with the private search and witness interviews, this undermines Arthur’s explanation of his knowledge. It strengthens the cumulative case without supplying an admission to the fatal blow.

deductions.title: The apparent Whitechapel connection
deductions.question: What might explain the arrangement in the yard?
deductions.explanation: The scarf arrangement recalls the paper’s invented illustration; Alden establishes post-mortem knife wounds, and George denies arranging the scarf. Arthur’s burned copy supplies a source for imitation. Read with the independent case against him, deliberate staging is supported as an inference, not a medical certainty or identification of the historical murderer.

pages.label: Temporary assignment
pages.heading: Temporary assignment
paragraphs: Inspectors Reed and Ellis,
You are temporarily assigned to the Whitechapel murder enquiry. We need additional officers to follow up the witness accounts received since the murder in Miller’s Court.

Constable Hale has arranged rooms for you at the Lantern. Mrs Baines is expecting Mr Reed and Mr Ellis this evening. She has not been told your occupation. Wear plain clothes and keep your assignment private while lodging there, so that your arrival does not become common talk.
Report to me at Commercial Street tomorrow morning for your assignments.

pages.label: The Whitechapel murders
pages.heading: The Whitechapel murders
pages.kicker: The Evening London Illustrated · Friday, 16 November 1888 · One penny
paragraphs: A week has passed since the murder in Miller’s Court, and the murderer is still at large. At the inquests, the surgeons have described throats cut and terrible injuries to the abdomen. Yet after all the questioning of witnesses and examination of suspected men, the police have brought no one to justice.
THE WHITECHAPEL HORRORS.—FROM AN IMAGINARY SKETCH.

The women of the district cannot stay indoors until Scotland Yard solves the case. Work must be found and rent paid. More constables are wanted in the courts and passages after dark; assurances from the authorities will not suffice.
pages.description: The newspaper’s woodcut shows a clothed woman lying in a yard with a scarf across her face.

travel-papers.title: Nora’s Bristol journey
travel-papers.format: Railway ticket, sleeve and family letter

pages.label: Ticket and addressed sleeve
paragraphs: G.W.R. · PADDINGTON TO BRISTOL · THIRD CLASS · SINGLE
Miss Nora Finch · The Lantern
Saturday, 17 November
pages.description: A small stiff card railway ticket rests beside its folded paper sleeve. The passenger name is handwritten on the sleeve, not printed on the ticket.

pages.label: A place in Bristol
paragraphs: My dear Nora,
I have spoken for you at the sewing room. They will try you on alterations on Monday, and I know they will keep you when they see your work.
Come on Saturday if you can. There is a room near mine, and you can stay with me until it is ready. Bring your sewing things. I have put Finch on the sleeve as you asked.
Write if the journey must wait. You need not explain everything on paper. I shall be glad to have you here.

pages.label: Work left at the workshop
paragraphs: Nora,
I have kept the unfinished seams at Shaw’s garment workshop. Do not turn back for them. Bring only what you need for the journey.
If you want me before you go, you know where to find me. I shall be at the long table by the window.

pages.label: The remaining photograph
pages.description: Nora stands beside an older woman in a studio portrait. A torn edge cuts through the space beside the bride.

pages.label: The reverse
paragraphs: Our wedding · 8 June 1884
pages.description: The handwritten date is intact on the reverse of the surviving card. No groom’s name remains.

pages.label: Work issued
pages.heading: Work issued
pages.description: A ruled work card with handwritten entries for cuffs and collars.

pages.label: The complete print
pages.description: A studio wedding portrait: Nora stands between an older woman and a man. All three figures and the edges of the print are intact.

pages.label: Maggie’s keepsake
paragraphs: Nora Finch and Arthur Vale · 8 June 1884
For Maggie
pages.description: The couple’s names, wedding date and dedication are handwritten on the reverse.

pages.label: Examination of Nora Vale
pages.heading: Examination of Nora Vale
paragraphs: At Constable Hale’s request I attended the rear yard of the Lantern, where I confirmed that Nora Vale was dead. She was subsequently removed for examination.
The injury to the head, caused by a hard, blunt blow, was the cause of death. The wounds to the throat and abdomen were inflicted after death.
These findings establish the order of the injuries, but not an exact hour of death. They do not identify a particular weapon or offender.
The knife wounds did not kill this woman. Resemblance to the reported Whitechapel murders does not establish that the same person was responsible.

pages.label: The readable portion
paragraphs: THE EVENING LONDON ILLUSTRATED
Friday, 16 November 1888
THE WHITECHAPEL MURDERS

A week has passed since the murder in Miller’s Court, and the murderer is still at large. At the inquests, the surgeons have described throats cut and terrible injuries to the abdomen. Yet after all the questioning of witnesses and examination of suspected men, the police have brought no one to justice.
THE WHITECHAPEL HORRORS.—FROM AN IMAGINARY SKETCH.
pages.description: A newspaper with burned edges. The masthead, date, article and woodcut remain visible; the woodcut shows a scarf across a woman’s face.

pages.label: From the Lantern
paragraphs: My dear friend,
The police have sent word of Nora’s death. I wanted you to hear from someone who knew her here as well. Their enquiry is complete, and they will write to you about it.
I shall help with her things when they may be released. Her sewing case is safe. She had your letter with the ticket and had made everything ready.
Mrs Baines is wearing the sleeve Nora mended yesterday. I thought you should know that she was working to the last, and speaking of the work you had found for her.
I am so sorry. I shall write again when I can tell you about the arrangements.

steps.label: Examine the ready luggage
steps.observation: A broad travelling trunk with iron bands and leather straps.

steps.label: Look over the coal cart
steps.observation: Coal sacks lie across the bed of the cart.

steps.label: Examine the repaired sleeve
steps.observation: Small, even stitches mend Mrs Baines’s worn sleeve. Nora’s needles and thread lie beside it.

steps.label: Look at the candlestick
steps.observation: The brass loop handle is bent and blue wax fills the dish.

steps.label: Read Maggie’s work note
steps.observation: Maggie has kept Nora’s unfinished seams at Shaw’s garment workshop. She can be found at the long table by the window.

steps.label: Open the trunk
steps.observation: A few travelling clothes lie loosely across the top.

steps.label: Lift the loose clothes
steps.observation: Stained bedclothes cover the bottom of the deep trunk.

steps.label: Examine the coal sacks
steps.observation: One sack sags over a hard object near the side of the cart.

steps.label: Lift the sack
steps.observation: A brass candlestick lies beneath it. The loop handle is bent; blue wax remains in the dish.
steps.blockedMessage: Ask Hale to keep the search private before lifting the sacks.

steps.label: Examine the bed and clothes
steps.observation: Clothes have been emptied beside the bed. Its blanket is missing and the rug is displaced.

steps.label: Lift the edge of the rug
steps.observation: Dark blood marks the floor beneath the rug.

steps.label: Open the sewing case
steps.observation: Thread, needles and cloth scraps surround a torn photograph in the lid.

steps.label: Examine the photograph
steps.observation: Nora and her mother remain. The person beside the bride has been torn away.

steps.label: Turn the photograph over
steps.observation: The remaining writing reads: “Our wedding · 8 June 1884”. No groom’s name remains.

steps.label: Follow the route to the yard
steps.observation: A short service landing and three broad, shallow steps can accommodate the large trunk.

steps.label: Look from Baines’s window
steps.observation: The landing and upper steps are visible. The projecting washhouse screens the discovery corner.

steps.label: Examine the hearth surface
steps.observation: Burned woollen clothing and partly burned paper remain among the ash.

steps.label: Separate the burned clothing
steps.observation: Stained woollen scraps remain among the ash.

steps.label: Unfold the surviving newspaper
steps.observation: The title, date and scarf illustration remain legible on a partly burned report.
steps.blockedMessage: Bring both investigators to help unfold the fragile newspaper.

steps.label: Examine the unfinished seams
steps.observation: Small, even stitches stop partway across the shirts.

reconstructions.title: What Baines could establish
reconstructions.instruction: Arrange only what Baines heard, saw and did. She could not identify the man.

events.label: Later, an unidentified man carries Nora’s trunk down the steps.
Baines withdraws, bolts her door and hides.
Baines hears voices, a cry and a thud from the rear rooms.

reconstructions.failure: Baines heard the disturbance, later saw the man with the trunk, then bolted her door and hid. She did not identify him.

steps.title: 17 November · Morning
steps.text: Reed and Ellis leave through the front door and report to Commercial Street. Later, a message from Constable Hale brings them back to the Lantern.

steps.speaker: hale
steps.text: Inspectors. The woman you met last night has been found dead. The doctor has attended; she has been taken to the mortuary.

steps.speaker: reed
steps.text: We will need everyone’s account, and the things left where they were found.

steps.speaker: hale
steps.text: The report is with the inspector. I’ll take Arthur to Commercial Street and keep him there while you search his lodging.

steps.title: The upstairs room
steps.text: Word has been sent to Bristol concerning Nora’s death. At Bell’s boot-repair shop, off Commercial Road, the landlord has admitted the officers to Arthur’s lodging.

steps.title: Commercial Street
steps.text: The recovered objects are brought to the station. The questions belong to the investigators, and the answers to Arthur.

steps.speaker: ellis
steps.text: We have the case before us. Let him answer each part of it.

steps.title: The same evening
steps.text: The report is complete. A police message has already been sent to Bristol. At the Lantern, Maggie has begun a personal letter to Nora’s sister.

steps.title: The Lantern
steps.text: The newspaper lies set aside. Maggie returns to the letter.
The common room carries on around the place where Nora worked.

ending: Nora’s case is complete. An urgent message has been sent to her sister. Maggie’s letter and Nora’s belongings will follow. At the Lantern, the newspaper is set aside and Maggie returns to her letter. The historical Whitechapel murders remain unresolved.
